messages:
oliver_devex: User report: `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood/repo.git@main` fails with resolver errors then falls back to trying to build wheels and errors out on macos/arm. They pasted: `ERROR: Could not build wheels for redwood-sdk, which is required to install pyproject.toml-based projects`

frank_engineer: thanks. Two things to check: 1) pyproject.build-system backend (poetry-core vs setuptools), 2) conflicting constraints from poetry.lock when installing via pip-from-vcs. Pip will ignore poetry.lock, but if our pyproject has constrained extras it can confuse resolver.

sana_pkg: also saw users hitting a poetry vs pip resolver conflict where `importlib-metadata` pinned by poetry.lock conflicts with a dependency requiring newer importlib on py3.11. When pip falls back to building from sdist it tries to compile and fails on arm because we don't ship wheels for that platform.

infra-bot: CI packaging job failed (job id 4622): wheel build step exited non-zero on macos-arm64. See logs: https://ci.internal/logs/4622

oliver_devex: there's also a support thread where `from redwood import AsyncClient` raised ImportError after a pip-installed wheel. Editable installs worked for them.

frank_engineer: editable installs mask package exports because they import from the repo directly. In sdist/wheel we might be missing the async module in package_data or not exporting it in `__init__.py`. Quick fix: add `from .async_client import AsyncClient` to `redwood/__init__.py` and include `redwood/py.typed` in the manifest.

sana_pkg: packaging checklist suggestion:
- ensure `pyproject.build-system` is compatible with pip-from-vcs (setuptools+wheel is safest) or document pip>=23 requirement for poetry-core
- include `py.typed` so typecheckers consume annotations
- add `tool.poetry.include` or MANIFEST.in entries for stubs/static files
- publish wheels for macos/arm and manylinux aarch64 using cibuildwheel to avoid local compiles

zoe_support: immediate workaround I gave users: upgrade pip & build tools, then build locally:
```
python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel build
python -m build
pip install dist/redwood-*.whl
```
For poetry users: `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes -o reqs.txt && pip install -r reqs.txt`

frank_engineer: longer term we should: add cibuildwheel to release workflow to publish universal2/manylinux wheels, add a CI smoke test that does a clean venv `pip install dist/*.whl` and then `python -c "from redwood import AsyncClient; import pkgutil; print(pkgutil.get_data('redwood','py.typed') is not None)"`

sana_pkg: small code/manifest suggestions: MANIFEST.in: `include redwood/py.typed\nrecursive-include redwood/static *` and in pyproject for poetry: `tool.poetry.include = [{"path": "redwood/py.typed"}]`

oliver_devex: can someone open a tiny PR that: switches build-system to setuptools+wheel (or documents the pip min version), adds py.typed, exports AsyncClient in __init__.py, and adds the CI smoke test? I'll hold the support ticket update until we have a patch or published wheel.

frank_engineer: will do a minimal PR with the exports + manifest + test. We'll leave cibuildwheel for follow-up since that's more infra work.

zoe_support: I'll draft KB article with the workarounds and the commands for both pip and poetry, include the note about lockfile vs VCS installs and recommending `poetry export` to make pip deterministic.

infra-bot: PR #1402 created with packaging fixes. CI run queued.

oliver_devex: awesome. Thanks all. Will update the user and mark the ticket pending. :thumbsup:
